_comment: DECLARED RULING/CODE PAIRS. A ruling document says what the estate does; a script does it. This
registry names the pairs so ops\audit-ruling-drift.ps1 can check that the code still agrees with
the document, which nothing did before 2026-09-06 (backlog E12).
ops\audit-twin-drift.ps1 covers CODE-to-CODE duplication - one rule implemented in two files. This
covers DOCUMENT-to-CODE: a ruling that changes without a deploy, and a script that does not notice.
Different failure, different registry, deliberately not merged.
EVERY ENTRY IS A DECISION SOMEONE DEFENDS IN A DIFF. `absent` means the symbol must NOT appear in
the file; `present` means it must. `why` is not decoration - an entry whose reason nobody can state
is an entry nobody can retire.

rulings.ruled: Brad, 2026-09-04: remove ALL hardcoded bands. The bands are specified per-run and could fluctuate, so should never be hard coded.
rulings.why: Section 3.3 of the brief: delete DEFAULT_COND once nothing reads them - a constant that exists is a constant something will use. It still states 350-650 cal in PROSE and resolve_conditions still falls back to it, so a run that states no conditions tells its machine gate one band and every agent a different one, silently. That exact defect already fired on hunt-2026-08-27-ten.
Section 3.2: `self.band = dict(band or DEFAULT_BAND)` must become a refusal. A band nobody typed is a band nobody agreed to, and two gates would enforce it silently for a whole run.
Section 3.3 names the harvest.py trio. A hard-coded 650 here once buried 1,556 candidates - 64% of the pool - against a band nobody had stated for that run.
